param: λ Human population logistic growth rate
K_H Human carrying capacity (logistic growth)
β Number of infectious bites delivered per vector per day (effective transmission term used in force of infection)

b Average biting rate per unit time of a female mosquito (appears in equations; paper text defines biting rate separately; set to 1.0 here because Table 2 provides β as infectious bites per vector per day)
M Number of alternative hosts besides humans in the environment
α_H Human progression rate Exposed→Infectious (inverse of human incubation time; Table 2 uses 3 days)
γ Human recovery rate Infectious→Recovered (inverse of recovery time; Table 2 uses 7 days)
e_V Number of eggs laid per female mosquito per unit time
τ_1 Egg development rate V1→V2 (inverse of egg development time; 3 days)
τ_2 Larval development rate V2→V3 (inverse of larval development time; 9 days)
τ_3 Pupal development rate V3→adult susceptible vectors (inverse of pupal development time; 3 days)
μ_1 Egg mortality rate
μ_2 Larval mortality rate (baseline)
μ_3 Pupal mortality rate
μ_V Adult female vector mortality rate
q Percentage of females among adult vectors
K_V Larval carrying capacity (logistic term applied to larvae stage V2)
κ Larvae mortality intensity due to limited carrying capacity (coefficient in density-dependent term κ*V2^2/K_V)
α_V Vector progression rate Exposed→Infectious (inverse of vector incubation time; Table 2 uses 10 days)
S_H(0) Initial human population (assumed initially susceptible except initial infections)
I_H(0) Initial infectious humans
N_V(0) Initial adult female vector population (total adults)
E_V(0) Initial exposed adult vectors
I_V(0) Initial infectious adult vectors
V_1(0) Initial eggs
V_2(0) Initial larvae
V_3(0) Initial pupae
